title: plsMD: a plasmid reconstruction tool from short-read assemblies
citation: Lotfi et al. 2026, BMC Bioinformatics, doi 10.1186/s12859-026-06585-y
what_it_is: The paper's own per-plasmid recall for plsMD, MOB-suite and gplas on its 80-isolate filtered benchmark (244 plasmids) and its 68-isolate novel set (269 plasmids). Values are copied from Additional file 2 and divided by 100.

tool_map_notes.gplas: The paper ran gplas; PlasBench's tool is gplas2 (its successor), so this pair is similar, not identical.

metrics.label: Per-plasmid recall
metrics.plasbench_source: {sample}/{tool}.per_plasmid.tsv, column completeness (matched on the truth plasmid accession)
metrics.note: plsMD's recall is the share of a reference plasmid's bases found in the reconstructed plasmid; PlasBench's completeness is the share of the truth plasmid's bases covered by aligned predicted sequence (MAPQ and identity filters apply). The same idea, not the same code.

caveats: plsMD's own tool column is the tool's published run on the paper's assemblies; a PlasBench run of plsmd uses your assembly, assembler and PLSDB release.
The filtered set was chosen by the authors for samples whose Unicycler assembly is explained by the closed genome, which favours every tool.
plsMD queries PLSDB, which probably contains the truth plasmids of the filtered set; the novel set is the paper's claim of absence from PLSDB 2024_05_31_v2, not verified here.

Truth plasmids are the paper's GenBank accessions; PlasBench's truth for the same isolate comes from the resolved assembly and is matched by accession, so a plasmid absent from it is reported as unmatched, not as zero.
